boom.name: Boom
boom.blurb: Markets are cheerful and companies are hiring.

slowdown.name: Slowdown
slowdown.blurb: Growth cools, hiring freezes and raises shrink.

crisis.name: Crisis
crisis.blurb: Markets crash, jobs get shaky and prices still rise.

smooth.name: A smooth ride
smooth.blurb: Steady weather all your life: no booms and no crashes.

crash30s.name: A crash in your 30s
crash30s.blurb: A crisis at 33 and 34 and a slowdown after it. Ordinary luck before and after.

lostDecade.name: A lost decade in your 40s
lostDecade.blurb: Ten sour years: slowdowns with a crisis in the middle. Ordinary luck around it.

lateCrash.name: A crash just before you retire
lateCrash.blurb: A crisis at 58 and 59, just as retirement at 60 comes into view. Ordinary luck before it.

provenance.basis: Illustrative four-state economy, tuned so the long-run mix is about 23% boom, 50% steady, 18% slowdown, 10% crisis. Inflation per regime averages about 4.5% across the mix (boom 5.1, steady 4.3, slowdown 3.8, crisis 5.3), so prices rise about 5.3 times over 38 years. It was 5.2% until the November 2026 review: that matched the 2012-2026 CPI average of about 5.6% but looked high for a 60-year view. 4.5% sits between the RBI's 4% target (band 2-6%) and the 4.9% average of the targeting era; recent years were lower (RBI put FY2025-26 near 2.1%) and FY2026-27 is projected near 5%. Sources are secondary summaries (RBI, Trading Economics, press), not checked against MoSPI. Crises last about 1.7 years on average. The scripts are fixed weather for Level 3: they replace the random draw in the ages they cover (the draw is still taken, so nothing else moves) and are illustrative. wageAdjPct is the extra raise (in percentage points) a fully cyclical job gets that year, averaging about zero across the mix.
